topic.subject: science
topic.title: Light, shadows and reflections
topic.scope: luminous and non-luminous objects, transparent/translucent/opaque, how shadows form, light travels in straight lines, pinhole camera

misconceptions.statement: The moon is a luminous object because it shines at night.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the act of being visible with the act of producing light.
misconceptions.fix: The moon is non-luminous; it only reflects the light coming from the sun.

probe.question: Which of these produces its own light: a candle, a mirror, or the moon?

misconceptions.why: Students associate 'transparent' with 'not there' because they can see through it clearly.
misconceptions.fix: Transparent objects are physical materials that allow light to pass through them, but they are still visible due to reflections and edges.

probe.question: If a glass window is transparent, can you see the window itself?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because light goes right through it.

misconceptions.statement: Light can bend around corners to reach dark areas.
misconceptions.why: Students observe light filling a room and assume it curves to reach all parts.
misconceptions.fix: Light travels in a straight line and cannot turn corners unless it is reflected by a surface.

probe.question: If you shine a torch into a bent pipe, will the light come out the other end?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, light will bend to follow the shape of the pipe.

misconceptions.statement: A shadow is a dark image of the object itself.
misconceptions.why: Students view the shadow as a 'copy' or 'ghost' of the object rather than an absence of light.
misconceptions.fix: A shadow is simply an area where light is blocked by an opaque object; it does not contain details of the object.

probe.question: Does a shadow of a person show their eyes and nose?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, if the shadow is clear enough.
